verses.text: Now on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene went early, while it was still dark, to the tomb, and saw the stone taken away from the tomb.
Therefore she ran and came to Simon Peter, and to the other disciple whom Jesus loved, and said to them, “They have taken away the Lord out of the tomb, and we don’t know where they have laid him!”
Therefore Peter and the other disciple went out, and they went toward the tomb.
They both ran together. The other disciple outran Peter, and came to the tomb first.
Stooping and looking in, he saw the linen cloths lying, yet he didn’t enter in.
Then Simon Peter came, following him, and entered into the tomb. He saw the linen cloths lying,
and the cloth that had been on his head, not lying with the linen cloths, but rolled up in a place by itself.
So then the other disciple who came first to the tomb also entered in, and he saw and believed.
For as yet they didn’t know the Scripture, that he must rise from the dead.
So the disciples went away again to their own homes.
But Mary was standing outside at the tomb weeping. So, as she wept, she stooped and looked into the tomb,
and she saw two angels in white sitting, one at the head, and one at the feet, where the body of Jesus had lain.

They told her, “Woman, why are you weeping?”
She said to them, “Because they have taken away my Lord, and I don’t know where they have laid him.”
When she had said this, she turned around and saw Jesus standing, and didn’t know that it was Jesus.

Jesus said to her,
“Woman, why are you weeping? Who are you looking for?”
She, supposing him to be the gardener, said to him, “Sir, if you have carried him away, tell me where you have laid him, and I will take him away.”

Jesus said to her,
“Mary.”
She turned and said to him, “Rabboni!” which is to say, “Teacher!”

Jesus said to her,
“Don’t hold me, for I haven’t yet ascended to my Father; but go to my brothers, and tell them, ‘I am ascending to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God.’”
Mary Magdalene came and told the disciples that she had seen the Lord, and that he had said these things to her.

When therefore it was evening, on that day, the first day of the week, and when the doors were locked where the disciples were assembled, for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in the middle, and said to them,
“Peace be to you.”
When he had said this, he showed them his hands and his side. The disciples therefore were glad when they saw the Lord.

Jesus therefore said to them again,
“Peace be to you. As the Father has sent me, even so I send you.”

When he had said this, he breathed on them, and said to them,
“Receive the Holy Spirit!
If you forgive anyone’s sins, they have been forgiven them. If you retain anyone’s sins, they have been retained.”
But Thomas, one of the twelve, called Didymus, wasn’t with them when Jesus came.

The other disciples therefore said to him, “We have seen the Lord!”
But he said to them, “Unless I see in his hands the print of the nails, put my finger into the print of the nails, and put my hand into his side, I will not believe.”

After eight days again his disciples were inside, and Thomas was with them. Jesus came, the doors being locked, and stood in the middle, and said,
“Peace be to you.”

Then he said to Thomas,
“Reach here your finger, and see my hands. Reach here your hand, and put it into my side. Don’t be unbelieving, but believing.”
Thomas answered him, “My Lord and my God!”

Jesus said to him,
“Because you have seen me,
you have believed. Blessed are those who have not seen, and have believed.”
Therefore Jesus did many other signs in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book;
but these are written, that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that believing you may have life in his name.

items.label: M1
items.outcome: arrival at the tomb
items.narrator: the evangelist, third-person, as informed reporter
items.paraphrase: Mary Magdalene travels to the burial site in the pre-dawn dark of the week's first day.
items.gloss: A grieving follower goes to tend a beloved teacher's grave before daylight — an act of devotion in a world where the story seems to have ended.
items.sitz: post-crucifixion mourning visit to a burial place, at first light

items.label: M2
items.substrate: the state of the stone being removed from the tomb
items.outcome: visual registration of the tomb's disturbed state
items.paraphrase: She perceives that the sealing stone is no longer in place.
items.gloss: What she came to do is arrested by what she finds; the grave has been touched by hands other than hers, and the visit turns into a discovery.
items.sitz: pre-dawn approach to a sealed rock-tomb

items.label: M3
items.substrate: Simon Peter and the other disciple whom Jesus loved (as destination)
items.outcome: arrival at the two disciples
items.paraphrase: She hurries back and reaches Simon Peter and the disciple Jesus loved.
items.gloss: The disturbance is too heavy to carry alone, so she brings it to those who share her attachment to the one buried here.
items.sitz: urgent report-carrying to fellow followers

items.label: M4
items.substrate: the embedded claim about the Lord's removal (M5)
items.outcome: the two disciples now hold her testimony
items.paraphrase: She reports to them what she has just seen.
items.gloss: A grieving woman becomes the first speaker of what has happened — the news enters the community only through her mouth.
items.sitz: eyewitness delivering a first-report to companions

items.label: M5
items.substrate: the Lord (his body) in the tomb
items.outcome: the Lord's body is no longer in the tomb
items.narrator: Mary Magdalene, within her reported speech, as inference from what she saw
items.paraphrase: Unnamed parties have removed the Lord's body from the burial place.
items.gloss: Without a body in view, the only frame she has for absence is theft; loss is being read as violation.
items.sitz: a mourner's inference from a disturbed grave

items.label: M6
items.substrate: the location where the Lord's body has been laid
items.outcome: an admitted gap in knowledge
items.narrator: Mary Magdalene, within her reported speech
items.paraphrase: The speaker and her companions lack knowledge of where the body has been placed.
items.gloss: The wound of the missing body is doubled by the wound of not knowing where he lies — she is cut off even from the small mercy of tending his corpse.
items.sitz: a mourner unable to complete burial-tending

items.label: M7
items.substrate: their prior location, with the tomb as destination
items.outcome: they are on their way to the tomb
items.paraphrase: Peter and the other disciple set out and head toward the burial place.
items.gloss: The alarming report doesn't paralyze them; loyalty pulls the disciples out toward the grave to see for themselves.
items.sitz: disciples responding to an alarming report

items.label: M8
items.outcome: joint rapid movement toward the tomb
items.paraphrase: The two run side by side along the way.
items.gloss: Two men moving together toward the same place — the urgency belongs to both, not to one.
items.sitz: urgency to verify a disturbing report

items.label: M9
items.outcome: the other disciple ahead of Peter
items.paraphrase: The other disciple pulls ahead of Peter.
items.gloss: For a moment the loyal pair becomes a pair being measured against each other; a small human ranking slips into a sacred errand.
items.sitz: two runners racing to a grave

items.label: M10
items.outcome: the other disciple present at the tomb before Peter
items.paraphrase: The other disciple reaches the burial place before Peter does.
items.gloss: The one who ran faster gets there first — an ordinary fact given quiet weight by who is being sought.
items.sitz: first witness reaching the disturbed grave

items.label: M11
items.outcome: a threshold view into the tomb without entry
items.paraphrase: He bends down and looks inside the burial chamber.
items.gloss: He goes as far as the threshold and no further; the body bends toward the grave but the will hangs back at its mouth.
items.sitz: a low-mouthed rock-tomb requiring stooping to see in

items.label: M12
items.substrate: the linen cloths lying in the tomb
items.outcome: visual registration of the abandoned wrappings
items.paraphrase: He notices the burial wrappings lying inside.
items.gloss: The linens are still there — the first hard fact he can add to her report, and it doesn't fit the theft she feared.
items.sitz: first inspection of a disturbed grave's interior

items.label: M13
items.substrate: the interior of the tomb (as threshold not crossed)
items.outcome: he remains outside
items.paraphrase: He refrains from crossing into the burial chamber.
items.gloss: He holds himself back at the entrance; reverence, or fear of defilement, or deference to Peter, keeps him from stepping in.
items.sitz: hesitation before a corpse-defiling space

items.label: M14
items.substrate: the path behind the other disciple, ending at the tomb
items.outcome: Peter present at the tomb
items.paraphrase: Peter arrives behind him at the burial place.
items.gloss: The slower runner arrives, and the pair is reunited at the same threshold — the order of speed reverses the order of entering.
items.sitz: the slower runner catching up

items.label: M15
items.outcome: Peter inside the tomb
items.paraphrase: Peter crosses the threshold into the burial chamber.
items.gloss: Where the other stopped, Peter walks in — the one who denied him is the first to cross into the place of his body.
items.sitz: the first entry into a disturbed grave

items.label: M16
items.substrate: the linen cloths lying in the tomb
items.outcome: Peter's visual registration of the wrappings from within
items.paraphrase: From inside, Peter notices the burial wrappings lying there.
items.gloss: From inside, the same linens the first man glimpsed at the door are seen straight on — the sight becomes a shared observation.
items.sitz: an interior inspection of a disturbed grave

items.label: M17
items.substrate: the head-cloth, folded up and lying separately from the other linens
items.outcome: registration of the distinct arrangement of the head-cloth
items.paraphrase: Peter also notes the head-covering set apart from the other wrappings, wrapped up in its own spot.
items.gloss: The second detail changes the register of the scene: the face-cloth folded off by itself is nobody's hurry, nobody's theft; someone has left this place in order.
items.sitz: careful inspection of a disturbed burial

items.label: M18
items.outcome: the other disciple inside the tomb
items.paraphrase: The disciple who had arrived first now also crosses into the burial chamber.
items.gloss: The hesitation at the door gives way; having seen Peter go in, the other disciple crosses too.
items.sitz: the first-arriver overcoming his earlier hesitation

items.label: M19
items.outcome: perception of the tomb's interior
items.paraphrase: Inside, he takes in what is there.
items.gloss: Now inside, he sees the arrangement for himself — no longer through the doorway but standing in the space where the body had been.
items.sitz: an interior look at the disturbed grave

items.label: M20
items.outcome: a state of belief
items.paraphrase: He comes to trust what he has seen.
items.gloss: The neatly folded cloths, without any explanation attached, are enough for him — belief here rests on what the eyes have gathered, not on anyone's teaching.
items.sitz: a follower's response to seeing the emptied grave

items.label: M21
items.substrate: the Scripture (specifically, the embedded claim M22)
items.outcome: an ignorance-state at this moment in the story
items.narrator: the evangelist, third-person, as retrospective aside
items.paraphrase: The narrator notes that the disciples had not yet grasped the scriptural claim about his rising.
items.gloss: The teller steps out of the scene to say plainly what the disciples themselves did not yet see: the scriptural key to what they were looking at had not yet been given them.
items.sitz: a later teller looking back on the disciples' pre-understanding

lineage.source_ref: Scripture (unspecified; likely Psalm 16:10, cf. Hosea 6:2 or Isaiah 53:10-11)
lineage.seam: The narrator invokes 'the Scripture' as a necessity-generating warrant for resurrection but leaves unsaid WHICH scriptural text is meant and

items.label: M22
items.substrate: the condition of being among the dead
items.outcome: rising out of the dead
items.narrator: Scripture, as reported by the evangelist
items.paraphrase: According to Scripture, his rising from among the dead is a necessity.
items.gloss: The empty grave is being reframed as required, not accidental — what happened here was written into Scripture before it was written into a garden.
items.sitz: scriptural necessity as understood by the later community

lineage.seam: The claim that he 'must' rise from the dead imports scriptural necessity language but leaves unsaid whether the source text itself framed ri

items.label: M23
items.substrate: the tomb (as origin), their own dwellings (as destination)
items.outcome: the disciples departed from the tomb toward home
items.paraphrase: The two disciples leave and head back to where they are staying.
items.gloss: The two go home; the discovery is real, but nothing has yet been said or seen that gathers them into praise or mission — the scene simply ends.
items.sitz: witnesses withdrawing after inspection

items.label: M24
items.outcome: Mary's continued presence at the tomb
items.paraphrase: Mary remains at the burial place, positioned just outside it.
items.gloss: The men leave; the grieving woman cannot — attachment holds her at the grave when reason would send her home.
items.sitz: a mourner who cannot leave the grave

items.label: M25
items.outcome: an ongoing weeping
items.paraphrase: She weeps while she stands there.
items.gloss: Her body keeps doing what mourners' bodies do; the vigil is not a plan but tears refusing to stop.
items.sitz: a mourner grieving at a disturbed grave

items.label: M26
items.outcome: a threshold view into the tomb
items.paraphrase: Still weeping, she bends down and looks into the burial chamber.
items.gloss: Through her weeping she finally does what the men did — she bends and looks in; grief and inquiry are happening in the same breath.
items.sitz: a mourner finally looking inside a low-mouthed rock-tomb

items.label: M27
items.substrate: two angels in white sitting at the head-position and foot-position of where Jesus' body had lain
items.outcome: visual encounter with the two angels
items.paraphrase: She sees two white-clad angels seated where the body had been, one where the head had lain and one where the feet had lain.
items.gloss: The empty space where his body lay is not empty; heavenly witnesses mark the head and foot of the absence and turn the grave into a kind of throne.
items.sitz: a mourner seeing heavenly figures inside a grave

items.label: M28
items.outcome: Mary is addressed with a question
items.paraphrase: The angels address her and ask why she is weeping.
items.gloss: The messengers do not deliver a message first; they ask about her tears, meeting her at the point of her grief rather than at the point of their news.
items.sitz: heavenly figures engaging a mourner

items.label: M29
items.outcome: a request for the cause of her lament
items.narrator: the two angels, within reported speech
items.paraphrase: The angels ask her the reason for her weeping.
items.gloss: The question makes her name her own sorrow — grief is being drawn into speech before it can be answered.
items.sitz: heavenly interlocutors probing a mourner's grief

items.label: M30
items.outcome: the angels receive her explanation
items.paraphrase: Mary replies to them.
items.gloss: She answers the heavenly figures as she would answer anyone — grief flattens the difference between an angel and a stranger.
items.sitz: a mourner answering heavenly figures

items.label: M31
items.outcome: her Lord is no longer where he was laid
items.paraphrase: Unnamed parties have removed her Lord from the burial place.
items.gloss: She repeats to the angels what she said to the disciples: the only frame she still has for his absence is that others took him.
items.sitz: a mourner's inference from a disturbed grave

items.label: M32
items.substrate: the location where they have laid him
items.outcome: an admitted gap in her knowledge
items.paraphrase: She herself does not know where they have placed him.
items.gloss: The pain has narrowed to a single unbearable point — not that he is dead, but that she cannot even find him.
items.sitz: a mourner unable to locate the missing body

items.label: M33
items.outcome: Mary now facing the other direction
items.paraphrase: Having spoken, she turns her body around.
items.gloss: Something behind her draws her attention; the vigil at the empty place breaks, and she turns toward whatever is there.
items.sitz: a mourner shifting her gaze from the tomb

items.label: M34
items.outcome: visual perception of a standing figure
items.narrator: the evangelist, third-person (knowing more than the character)
items.paraphrase: She notices a man standing there.
items.gloss: There is a person present she had not registered — the encounter begins as a plain sighting of a stranger.
items.sitz: a mourner meeting an unrecognized figure at the grave

items.label: M35
items.outcome: a state of misrecognition
items.paraphrase: She fails to recognize who the man is.
items.gloss: Sight alone is not enough; she is looking straight at him and does not know him — grief and expectation have made the beloved unrecognizable.
items.sitz: a mourner failing to identify the risen one

items.label: M36
items.outcome: not-stated
items.narrator: the evangelist (as narrator-knowledge disclosed inside Mary's non-knowledge)
items.paraphrase: The figure she is seeing is in fact Jesus.
items.gloss: The teller quietly tells the reader what she cannot yet see; we are let into an identity she is still missing.
items.sitz: the teller's superior knowledge about the risen one

items.label: M37
items.outcome: Mary is addressed
items.paraphrase: Jesus addresses her with two questions.
items.gloss: He does not name himself; he opens with questions, letting her speak before he is known.
items.sitz: the risen one initiating dialogue

items.label: M38
items.outcome: a request for the cause of her lament
items.paraphrase: He asks her why she is weeping.
items.gloss: The same question the angels asked is now put by him — her tears are being taken seriously twice over before any comfort is offered.
items.sitz: the risen one probing a mourner's grief

items.label: M39
items.outcome: a request to name whom she seeks
items.paraphrase: He asks her whom she is looking for.
items.gloss: The second question sharpens the first: her weeping is being read as a search — grief here is a form of looking for someone.
items.sitz: the risen one probing what a mourner wants

items.label: M40
items.outcome: a mistaken cognition-state about who he is
items.paraphrase: She takes the man before her to be the gardener.
items.gloss: The most obvious explanation for a man in a garden at dawn is the man who tends the garden — she reaches for the ordinary because the ordinary is all she can bear.
items.sitz: a mourner defaulting to the most plausible identity in a garden-tomb

lineage.seam: Is the text standing on the Eden garden here — staging the risen Jesus as a 'gardener' beside a tomb-in-a-garden as a new-creation echo — an

items.label: M41
items.outcome: not-stated
items.narrator: Mary's supposition, reported by the evangelist
items.paraphrase: The figure is, in her supposition, the caretaker of the garden.
items.gloss: The wrong identification lets her keep going; she treats the risen one as a workman and, on that misreading, is able to ask her question.
items.sitz: a plausible identity in a tomb-garden

items.label: M42
items.substrate: the embedded request (M43) and its accompanying promise (M44)
items.outcome: the supposed gardener is petitioned
items.paraphrase: She addresses him and asks him — on the condition that he took the body — to disclose where it is, so she can retrieve it.
items.gloss: She addresses him as she would a caretaker — asking, on the chance that he was the one who moved the body, to be told where.
items.sitz: a mourner petitioning a supposed caretaker

items.label: M43
items.substrate: the location where he laid the body
items.outcome: disclosure of the body's location to Mary
items.paraphrase: She asks him — if he was the one who moved the body — to disclose to her where he placed it.
items.gloss: The petition is a mourner's — she is still trying to complete the burial, and any information at all would be a mercy.
items.sitz: a petition conditional on the addressee having done the moving

items.label: M44
items.outcome: the body relocated by Mary
items.paraphrase: She promises that she herself will remove the body.
items.gloss: She commits to carrying the body away herself — a promise beyond her strength, spoken because love does not measure.
items.sitz: a mourner offering to complete burial-tending herself

items.label: M45
items.outcome: Mary is summoned by name
items.paraphrase: Jesus calls her by name.
items.gloss: One word — her name — does what argument and evidence cannot; the beloved is known through being addressed by name.
items.sitz: the risen one naming his own by name

items.label: M46
items.outcome: Mary now oriented toward Jesus
items.paraphrase: She turns toward him.
items.gloss: The name reaches through the misrecognition; her whole body turns because something in her has already recognized who is speaking.
items.sitz: recognition prompting a bodily reorientation

items.label: M47
items.substrate: Jesus (addressed with the Aramaic term for 'teacher')
items.outcome: Jesus is named as teacher
items.paraphrase: She responds by addressing him as her teacher, in Aramaic.
items.gloss: She answers him not with a title of majesty but with the word a student uses for her teacher — the relationship resumes where it left off.
items.sitz: a disciple recognizing her teacher

items.label: M48
items.substrate: the Aramaic term Mary used in M47
items.outcome: the term rendered accessible to a non-Aramaic audience
items.narrator: the evangelist, third-person, as translator for the audience
items.paraphrase: The narrator glosses the Aramaic term she used with its equivalent for the audience.
items.gloss: The teller pauses to translate for readers who do not share her language — the intimacy of the address is preserved by being explained.
items.sitz: a teller addressing an audience for whom Aramaic is not native

items.label: M49
items.substrate: the embedded prohibition, commission, and announcement (M50, M52, M53)
items.outcome: Mary receives his speech
items.paraphrase: Jesus speaks to her with a series of instructions and an announcement.
items.gloss: Reunion does not settle into embrace; almost at once he begins to speak, and his words start reshaping what her recognition means.
items.sitz: the risen one commissioning his witness

items.label: M50
items.outcome: Mary refraining from holding him
items.paraphrase: He forbids her to cling to him, giving as his reason that he has not yet gone up to the Father.
items.gloss: The one she has just found back is not to be gripped and kept; presence here is real but on its way toward the Father, and love has to learn to hold it that way.
items.sitz: a risen one who is in transit toward the Father

items.label: M51
items.substrate: the group Jesus names 'my brothers' (as destination)
items.outcome: Mary set on her way to them
items.paraphrase: He commands her to go to those he calls his brothers.
items.gloss: She is turned away from him and toward the others — and the others are called brothers, drawing them into the very sonship he has with the Father.
items.sitz: a risen one commissioning his witness

items.label: M52
items.substrate: the further embedded announcement (M54) to be delivered to the brothers
items.outcome: the announcement conveyed to the brothers
items.paraphrase: He commands her to deliver a message to them.
items.gloss: He does not go to the disciples himself; he entrusts a message to her, and her recognition becomes an errand.
items.sitz: a risen one entrusting a witness with a message

items.label: M53
items.outcome: arrival with the one named 'my Father and your Father, my God and your God'
items.narrator: Jesus, within a doubly-embedded reported speech
items.paraphrase: He announces that he is going up to the one who is his and their Father, his and their God.
items.gloss: The message is that his going to the Father is also their going — his God has become theirs, and the family of the Father has widened to include them.
items.sitz: a risen one declaring his transition to the Father

lineage.seam: Is the paired possessive formula ('my Father and your Father, my God and your God') standing on Ruth's covenantal 'your people my people, yo

items.label: M54
items.outcome: Mary present with the disciples
items.paraphrase: Mary Magdalene reaches the disciples.
items.gloss: She does what she was told to do; the woman who came to a grave now comes to a circle, carrying news instead of spices.
items.sitz: a commissioned witness carrying out her sending

items.label: M55
items.substrate: the two embedded reports to the disciples (M57 and M58)
items.outcome: the disciples receive her testimony
items.paraphrase: She reports to them what happened at the tomb and what he told her.
items.gloss: She becomes, in fact, the first apostle — the first to deliver an account of the risen one to his gathered followers.
items.sitz: the first witness delivering resurrection-testimony to the circle

items.label: M56
items.outcome: a completed sighting of the Lord
items.paraphrase: She reports that she has seen the Lord.
items.gloss: Her testimony is grounded in her own eyes; it is not something she was told but something she saw, and that is the ground on which she stands.
items.sitz: a witness naming her firsthand encounter

items.label: M57
items.substrate: the words previously spoken to Mary (referring back to Jesus's speech in M49-M54)
items.outcome: Mary was addressed with these words
items.paraphrase: She reports that he had spoken these things to her.
items.gloss: Alongside the sighting, she carries the words he entrusted to her; message and eyewitness are being delivered together.
items.sitz: a witness relaying that words were spoken and their content

items.label: M58
items.substrate: the room where they were meeting
items.outcome: the disciples enclosed together, hidden from outside view
items.paraphrase: That evening, on the first day of the week, the disciples were gathered behind bolted doors out of fear of the Judean authorities.
items.gloss: The circle is still living inside the crucifixion — hiding, bolted in, believing themselves next; the good news has not yet reshaped their sense of danger.
items.sitz: followers of an executed teacher hiding from local authorities on the evening of the first day of the week
items.paradigm: fearful hiding of a persecuted group

items.label: M59
items.substrate: the location of the assembled disciples
items.outcome: Jesus present among them
items.paraphrase: Jesus arrives where they are.
items.gloss: He does not wait to be let in; presence arrives into a locked room, meeting fear where fear has barricaded itself.
items.sitz: a risen one appearing to a hidden circle

items.label: M60
items.substrate: the middle of the assembled group
items.outcome: Jesus stationed at the center of the group
items.paraphrase: He takes a position among them.
items.gloss: He plants himself in the middle of them — not at the edge, not passing through, but centered among the ones who had scattered.
items.sitz: a risen one visibly placing himself among his followers

items.label: M61
items.outcome: the disciples are greeted
items.paraphrase: He addresses them with a greeting.
items.gloss: The first thing he offers is speech, not rebuke — the fear behind their locked doors is met with address.
items.sitz: a risen one greeting his followers

items.label: M62
items.outcome: not-stated
items.paraphrase: He wishes peace upon them.
items.gloss: A common greeting is spoken, but from this mouth 'peace' is not a courtesy — it is the thing being handed to them by the one they saw killed.
items.sitz: a customary greeting-blessing, freighted here by the speaker's identity

items.label: M63
items.outcome: the wounded parts of his body visible to the disciples
items.paraphrase: He displays to them his hands and his side.
items.gloss: He offers the marks of the crucifixion as the proof of who he is; the risen body is being recognized precisely as the wounded one.
items.sitz: a risen one making his crucified body identifiable

items.label: M64
items.outcome: visual recognition of the Lord
items.paraphrase: The disciples recognize him as the Lord upon seeing him.
items.gloss: Sight of the wounded body is what turns them from a hidden group into people who know him; their eyes settle a question their ears had not.
items.sitz: followers identifying their risen teacher

items.label: M65
items.outcome: a state of gladness in the disciples
items.paraphrase: They become glad in response.
items.gloss: Fear breaks into joy; a room that had been sealed against death fills with the response of people whose grief has been overturned.
items.sitz: followers moving from fear to joy at recognition

items.label: M66
items.outcome: the disciples receive his second address
items.paraphrase: Jesus addresses them a second time with a greeting and a sending.
items.gloss: Joy is not the endpoint; almost at once he speaks again, turning a reunion into a sending.
items.sitz: a risen one turning greeting into commissioning

items.label: M67
items.outcome: not-stated
items.paraphrase: He again wishes peace upon them.
items.gloss: Peace is spoken again, this time as the ground on which they will be sent — the sending starts from the same word that met their fear.
items.sitz: a peace-greeting repeated to open a commissioning

items.label: M68
items.outcome: the disciples sent as he was sent by the Father
items.paraphrase: He sends them out, aligning his sending of them with the Father's sending of him.
items.gloss: His own commissioning by the Father becomes theirs; the pattern of his sending is now the pattern of their sending.
items.sitz: a risen one extending his own commissioning to his followers

items.label: M69
items.outcome: the disciples receive his breath on them
items.paraphrase: He blows his breath onto them.
items.gloss: He breathes on them — the small physical act carries the weight of the first breath given to the human creature; a new creation is being gestured toward.
items.sitz: a symbolic breath-conferral echoing a life-giving act

lineage.seam: Imports the creator's breath-giving act as the shape of Jesus's insufflation of the disciples, but leaves unsaid whether this is a second cr

items.label: M70
items.substrate: the embedded imperative and conditional authorizations (M72, M73, M74)
items.outcome: the disciples receive his instruction
items.paraphrase: He speaks to them again, issuing a command and two conditional authorizations.
items.gloss: The breath is not left silent; it is joined to speech that names what has just been given and what it authorizes them to do.
items.sitz: a risen one paired-conferring breath and authority

items.label: M71
items.outcome: the Holy Spirit received by the disciples
items.paraphrase: He commands them to take the Holy Spirit into themselves.
items.gloss: The Spirit is not something they achieve or await; it is being handed over as a gift already breathed into them, on command.
items.sitz: a risen one conferring the promised Spirit on his followers

lineage.seam: Is the command to receive breath/spirit standing on Ezekiel's valley-of-dry-bones oracle where breath is summoned into the slain, and if so

items.label: M72
items.outcome: those sins stand forgiven for those persons
items.paraphrase: He tells them that when they release someone's sins, those sins stand released.
items.gloss: The mercy he embodied is being placed in their hands; their release of another's sins will carry the weight of his own release.
items.sitz: a risen one delegating a judicial-mercy authority

lineage.seam: Is the paired forgive/retain authorization standing on the Isaian key-of-David 'open/shut' tradition of delegated binding authority, and if

items.label: M73
items.outcome: those sins stand retained for those persons
items.paraphrase: He tells them that when they hold someone's sins in place, those sins stand held.
items.gloss: The counterpart is spoken plainly: to hold back release is also a real act; the authority given is not only sweet but weighty.
items.sitz: a risen one delegating the counterpart authority to withhold release

items.label: M74
items.agent: Thomas (one of the twelve, called the Twin)
items.substrate: the rest of the disciples at the moment of Jesus's coming
items.outcome: Thomas outside the circle of witnesses to this appearance
items.narrator: the evangelist, third-person, as retrospective aside setting up the next scene
items.paraphrase: Thomas, one of the twelve and nicknamed the Twin, was absent from the group during the appearance.
items.gloss: The teller notes that one of the inner circle was not there — the story is honest about who did and did not see, and marks the gap.
items.sitz: a teller noting a member of the twelve was missing from a decisive event

items.label: M75
items.substrate: the embedded testimony (M77) delivered to Thomas
items.outcome: Thomas receives their testimony
items.paraphrase: The other disciples report to Thomas that they have seen the Lord.
items.gloss: The others do what Mary did for them: they carry the news of the sighting to the one who was absent.
items.sitz: witnesses relaying a resurrection-appearance to the absent one

items.label: M76
items.outcome: a completed sighting of the Lord
items.narrator: the other disciples, within their reported speech
items.paraphrase: They claim to have had a firsthand sighting of the Lord.
items.gloss: Their claim is anchored in their own eyes — the same ground that convinced them is what they now stand on with him.
items.sitz: witnesses naming their firsthand encounter

items.label: M77
items.outcome: the other disciples receive his terms
items.paraphrase: Thomas replies to them with the terms on which he will believe.
items.gloss: Thomas does not simply refuse; he replies, and lays down the terms on which he will and will not be moved.
items.sitz: a doubter setting verification-terms against a communal testimony

items.label: M78
items.substrate: the disciples' claim that they have seen the Lord
items.outcome: a refusal to believe pending the specified conditions
items.paraphrase: He declares he will withhold belief until he can inspect the nail-marks by sight, probe them with his finger, and place his hand in the side-wound.
items.gloss: He insists that testimony from friends is not enough; belief will have to rest on his own hands and his own eyes finding the wounds themselves.
items.sitz: a demand for tactile-visual verification of the crucifixion-wounds on the risen body

items.label: M79
items.substrate: the indoor space where they meet
items.outcome: the disciples, including Thomas, gathered inside
items.paraphrase: After a week, the disciples are again gathered indoors, and this time Thomas is present.
items.gloss: A week passes; the same room, the same door, but this time the doubter is inside — the story circles back to give him what he asked for.
items.sitz: a second gathering of the circle eight days later

items.label: M80
items.substrate: the location of the assembled disciples
items.outcome: Jesus present among them
items.paraphrase: Jesus arrives among them despite the shut doors.
items.gloss: Once again the shut door is no obstacle; presence enters where fear had sealed itself in.
items.sitz: a risen one appearing again inside a shut room

items.label: M81
items.substrate: the middle of the assembled group
items.outcome: Jesus stationed at the center
items.paraphrase: He takes his place at the center of the group.
items.gloss: He again places himself at the center of the group — the same posture, offered a second time so that the one who missed it before is now included.
items.sitz: a risen one visibly placing himself among his followers

items.label: M82
items.outcome: the disciples are greeted
items.paraphrase: He greets them.
items.gloss: He begins as he did the first time — with speech, with greeting, not with reproof.
items.sitz: a risen one repeating the peace-greeting

items.label: M83
items.outcome: not-stated
items.paraphrase: He wishes peace upon them.
items.gloss: The same peace-word is offered again; the pattern is being repeated so that Thomas hears with his own ears what the others heard.
items.sitz: a peace-greeting inside the second appearance

items.label: M84
items.substrate: the embedded directives to Thomas (M86, M87, M88, M89, M90)
items.outcome: Thomas is addressed with a series of instructions
items.paraphrase: He then turns and speaks directly to Thomas.
items.gloss: The greeting made to the group narrows to a direct address to the one who set the terms; he is met by name and singled out.
items.sitz: a risen one meeting a doubter on the doubter's stated terms

items.label: M85
items.outcome: Thomas's finger extended toward Jesus
items.paraphrase: He tells Thomas to extend his finger toward him.
items.gloss: The exact test Thomas demanded is being offered to him — his conditions are neither refused nor scolded, simply met.
items.sitz: an invitation to tactile inspection matching the doubter's terms

items.label: M86
items.outcome: Thomas's visual inspection of Jesus's hands
items.paraphrase: He tells Thomas to look at his hands.
items.gloss: Look, he says — the seeing Thomas asked for is placed in front of him.
items.sitz: an invitation to visual inspection of the wounds

items.label: M87
items.outcome: Thomas's hand extended toward Jesus
items.paraphrase: He tells Thomas to extend his hand toward him.
items.gloss: The invitation continues: not only look, but reach — the space between them is being closed on Thomas's own terms.
items.sitz: a further tactile invitation

items.label: M88
items.substrate: Thomas's hand, placed into Jesus's side
items.outcome: Thomas's hand inside the side-wound
items.paraphrase: He tells Thomas to place that hand into the wound in his side.
items.gloss: The deepest condition he named — hand in the side-wound — is not disallowed but offered; the risen body opens itself even to that touch.
items.sitz: the deepest tactile verification, matching Thomas's stated terms

items.label: M89
items.outcome: a state of belief in Thomas
items.paraphrase: He commands him to shift from disbelief into belief.
items.gloss: The verification is only the doorway; what is really being asked of him is a change of state — to stop refusing and to trust.
items.sitz: a summons to complete the movement the verification enables

items.label: M90
items.outcome: Jesus is addressed with Thomas's response
items.paraphrase: Thomas responds by addressing him.
items.gloss: Thomas speaks — the doubter's next move is not to reach out but to answer with words.
items.sitz: a doubter answering with a confession

items.label: M91
items.outcome: not-stated
items.paraphrase: He names Jesus as his Lord and his God.
items.gloss: What comes out is not a report of touch but the highest possible naming — a doubter's first sentence is a confession of God.
items.sitz: a follower's acclamatory confession of the risen one

lineage.seam: Is Thomas's paired acclamation 'my Lord and my God' standing on the Psalmist's cry 'my God and my Lord' as covenantal address to YHWH, and i

items.label: M92
items.outcome: Thomas receives his reply
items.paraphrase: Jesus replies to him with an evaluation and a beatitude.
items.gloss: He does not simply accept the confession; he uses it to open a wider window — his reply reaches past Thomas toward everyone who will come later.
items.sitz: the risen one commenting on the belief-through-seeing pattern

items.label: M93
items.outcome: Thomas now in a state of belief, grounded in having seen
items.paraphrase: He evaluates that Thomas has come to belief on the ground of having seen him.
items.gloss: He names honestly what has happened here: this belief came by sight — a real belief, but tied to what the eyes were given.
items.sitz: an evaluation of belief-via-sight

items.label: M94
items.outcome: not-stated
items.paraphrase: He pronounces a blessing on those who come to belief without seeing.
items.gloss: The blessing tilts toward the ones who will never get this room, this body, these wounds; their believing without seeing is being honored in advance.
items.sitz: a benediction on the not-yet-eyewitness generation of believers

items.label: M95
items.substrate: further sign-events performed before the disciples
items.outcome: a body of witnessed signs beyond those in this account
items.narrator: the evangelist, third-person, as book-summary aside
items.paraphrase: The narrator asserts that Jesus performed many further signs in the presence of his followers beyond the ones he has recorded.
items.gloss: The teller lifts his head from the scene to say that what he has shown is a selection — much more happened than he has set down.
items.sitz: a teller concluding a written account by pointing beyond what he included

items.label: M96
items.outcome: a written record that excludes them
items.narrator: the evangelist, third-person, as book-summary aside
items.paraphrase: He notes that those further signs are absent from the present writing.
items.gloss: He admits plainly that what is missing from the book is missing on purpose — the record is honest about being partial.
items.sitz: a teller marking the limits of his own written selection

items.label: M97
items.agent: these things (the accounts he has selected)
items.outcome: a written record aimed at the reader's believing (M99) and living (M101)
items.narrator: the evangelist, third-person, as book-purpose statement
items.paraphrase: He notes that what he has written was written for a specific purpose regarding the reader.
items.gloss: The selection is not idle; it was made with the reader in mind, aimed at a particular outcome in the one who is reading.
items.sitz: a teller declaring the purpose of his written selection

items.label: M98
items.outcome: the reader in a state of belief in that claim
items.paraphrase: The intended purpose is that the reader come to believe a specific claim about Jesus.
items.gloss: The reader is being addressed directly — the book itself is asking to move the one holding it from watching the story to trusting its claim.
items.sitz: a teller naming reader-belief as the intended effect of his book

items.label: M99
items.outcome: not-stated
items.paraphrase: The claim to be believed identifies Jesus as the Christ and as the Son of God.
items.gloss: The trust being asked for is not vague warmth; it is the confession that this Jesus is both the promised one and the Son of God.
items.sitz: a first-century identity-claim binding two titles onto Jesus

lineage.seam: Imports the royal-messianic 'Christ / Son of God' titulature as the content of saving belief, but leaves unsaid whether the source's own sen

items.label: M100
items.substrate: the reader's condition apart from life-in-his-name
items.outcome: life possessed by the reader, held in the name of Jesus
items.paraphrase: The further intended purpose is that, through such believing, the reader may have life in his name.
items.gloss: Belief is not the endpoint either; the whole aim reaches past belief to life — and that life is offered to the reader through his name.
items.sitz: a teller naming reader-life as the further intended effect of belief

reception.title: The resurrection end-silence — how it was received

readers.label: Lake
readers.reading: Lake treats the women's silence as the deliberate, emphatic main point of Mark's ending, while allowing that a now-lost continuation likely explained how they eventually spoke.
readers.quoted_span: the deliberate silence of the women at the beginning — which is the main point — is perfectly plain, for the statement is quite emphatic

readers.label: Orr (1908)
readers.reading: Orr acknowledges Mark breaks off at the women's flight in trembling, but insists Mark's Gospel nonetheless implied — no less than the others — that a report followed.
readers.quoted_span: St. Mark breaks off with the women fleeing from the tomb in "trembling and astonishment" ; but there can be no reasonable doubt that his Gospel also, not less than the others, contemplated a report of t

readers.label: Mark · ICC
readers.reading: Gould normalizes the abrupt ending as consistent with Mark's habitual brevity at the gospel's margins — not strange, not requiring explanation, simply characteristic.
readers.quoted_span: Mark gives merely the announcement of the resurrection to the women by the angels, and closes with this. This, instead of being strange, and requiring explanation, is quite in accordance with the character of Mark

readers.label: Matthew · ICC
readers.reading: Allen reads Mark's silence as naturally inviting a follow-up appearance; Matthew, uneasy with it, rewrites the women as speaking, then continues with the appearance — but unmotivated.
readers.quoted_span: It is very natural that this should have been followed by an appearance to them of Christ dispelling their fear and repeating the angel's message. Mt. alters "and told no one," etc., into "ran to tell His disciples."

readers.label: Longer Ending (16:9–20)
readers.reading: The most consequential reception act: a later hand SUPPLIED an ending — appearances + commission + ascension — precisely because Mark's abrupt 16:8 silence was felt as a gap that had to be closed.

readers.label: Shorter Ending
readers.reading: A second, briefer supplied ending in some manuscripts — independent evidence that the 16:8 silence generated MULTIPLE closure-attempts, not one.

readers.label: Narrative criticism
readers.reading: Reads 16:8 not as a defect or accident but as an INTENTIONAL narrative choice — the silence forces the reader to supply the continuation (the 'hermeneutic of secrecy'). NOT in our corpus (the narrative-critical register is a known coverage gap, IRR228) — added as attested/inferred.

center.label: Mark 16:8 — the end-silence
center.reading: Each account ends on a silence; Mark breaks off abruptly with the women afraid and saying nothing. What happens after is unnarrated, later supplied, or left open — the meaty end-gap.
center.title: The resurrection end-silence (Mark 16:8 · the unnarrated after)

cross_gospel.seam: comparative beats key on narrative beat + carried_by gospel; no verse or move handle joins a beat to the reader's selection. Method seam item (SS E requirement (a)/(b), SS I).
cross_gospel.seam_reader: the four gospels are lined up by episode, not verse by verse, so an episode cannot yet be matched to the verse you are reading.

beats.beat: female follower(s) travel to the tomb early on the first day
beats.note: MATT names two Marys; MARK three women with spices; LUKE a group with spices; JOHN Mary Magdalene alone

beats.beat: the sealing stone is found/made displaced from the tomb entrance
beats.note: MATT dramatizes an angel rolling it in real time; MARK/LUKE/JOHN find it already moved (divine passive)

beats.beat: the women/witness(es) enter or peer into the tomb
beats.note: MARK and LUKE enter bodily; JOHN has the disciples enter and Mary bend down to look; MATT omits an interior entry

beats.beat: the body of Jesus is discovered absent from its burial place
beats.note: framed as angelic declaration in MATT/MARK/LUKE and as empirical discovery-then-report in JOHN

beats.beat: one or more numinous figures (angel/young man/two men) are present at the tomb
beats.note: MATT one angel outside; MARK one young man inside; LUKE and JOHN two figures; JOHN's appear only in Mary's second visit

beats.beat: the numinous figure(s) are visually marked by whiteness/dazzling appearance
beats.note: lightning/snow (MATT), white robe (MARK), dazzling clothes (LUKE), white (JOHN)

beats.beat: the witnesses react with fear, dread, or bewilderment
beats.note: MATT guards struck down + women's mingled fear/joy; MARK alarm/terror; LUKE terror + bowing; JOHN grief rather than terror

beats.beat: the figure(s) address the witnesses with a speech-act interpreting the empty tomb
beats.note: MATT/MARK a commission; LUKE a rhetorical rebuke + reminder; JOHN only a 'why do you weep' question

beats.beat: the sought one is identified as the crucified Jesus
beats.note: MATT/MARK by the angelic naming, LUKE embedded in the passion-prediction; JOHN never verbalizes crucifixion in this scene

beats.beat: his absence from the tomb is explicitly declared ('he is not here')
beats.note: formulaic in the synoptics; JOHN dramatizes absence but never states the formula

beats.beat: his resurrected/raised status is announced (typically as divine passive)
beats.note: MATT/MARK/LUKE via the figures' proclamation; JOHN gestures at it only through the beloved disciple's belief and a scriptural aside

beats.beat: the witnesses are invited to view/verify the vacated burial spot
beats.note: MATT/MARK by directive ('come, see'); LUKE by finding no body; JOHN by inspection of the linen wrappings

beats.beat: a prior word of Jesus is invoked to frame what has happened
beats.note: MATT/MARK cite his earlier promise about Galilee; LUKE cites the passion-and-resurrection prediction; JOHN cites scripture instead

beats.beat: the witnesses depart from the tomb
beats.note: MATT hasten with fear+joy; MARK flee in terror; LUKE return to the eleven; JOHN Mary runs to Peter, disciples return home

beats.beat: the witnesses are commissioned/moved to report to the (male) disciples
beats.note: explicit commission in MATT/MARK; LUKE self-initiated report; JOHN Mary's spontaneous run to Peter/beloved disciple

beats.beat: the announcement is (or is to be) carried to Peter and the wider disciple circle
beats.note: MARK names Peter in the commission (and shorter ending); LUKE the eleven; JOHN Peter and the beloved disciple; MATT names 'his disciples' without Peter

beats.beat: a promise of future seeing/reunion with the risen Jesus is issued
beats.note: both locate it in Galilee via a 'he goes before you' formula; absent from LUKE and JOHN's tomb scene

beats.beat: male disciple(s) go to the tomb to verify the women's report
beats.note: LUKE Peter alone; JOHN Peter with the beloved disciple in a footrace

beats.beat: the linen burial cloths are seen lying in the tomb
beats.note: LUKE a single mention by Peter; JOHN elaborated as wrappings plus separately rolled head-cloth

beats.beat: a closing cognitive/affective state is left unresolved into full belief
beats.note: MARK women's fearful silence; LUKE Peter's amazement; contrast JOHN's beloved-disciple belief and MATT's commissioned joy
